newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Sudan says Eritrea and Israel plan to cut key road.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says Eritrea and Israel plan to cut key road.

text.p: Sudan's ambassador to Ethiopia was quoted on Wednesday as saying Eritrean troops were planning, with Israeli help, to cut the only road linking Khartoum to the Red Sea.
"There is information there has been a build up by Eritrean troops with the intent of cutting the road between Port Sudan and Khartoum," Ambassador Osman al-Sayed told an Addis Ababa newspaper.

"We also know for a fact there are experts from Israel giving advice and instructions to the Eritreans," he added. "This is completely unacceptable. We are ready and will always defend our territory."
Eritrea and Uganda have denied repeated accusations from Sudan's Islamist-backed government that Eritrean and Ugandan government troops have invaded Sudan in support of Sudanese rebels.
"At this very moment, there are Eritrean troops inside Sudan occupying Sudanese territory and at another corner Ugandan troops have entered Sudanese territory," the ambassador said.
He said he was optimistic relations between Khartoum and Addis Ababa would improve as both wanted to solve problems.
The Ethiopian government accused Khartoum of harbouring gunmen who attempted to assassinate Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa in 1995. Their relations have been frosty since.
Eritrea broke off diplomatic relations with Sudan in December 1994, accusing Khartoum of sending Moslem fundamentalists across their common border to destabilise the Red Sea state.
It gave the former Sudanese embassy in the Eritrean capital Asmara to an alliance of Sudanese rebels as a headquarters.
